source.title: Sparsity, Superposition, and Forgetting: A Mechanistic Study of Representation Retention in Continual Learning
source.authors: Jan Wasilewski; Jȩdrzej Kozal; Micha l Woźniak; Bartosz Krawczyk

record.file_problem: The full paper is present, but the extracted text has some garbled equations, broken words, and incomplete-looking table formatting.
record.tranche_reason: It measures feature-direction overlap in a controlled toy network to study superposition under sparse inputs and a latent bottleneck, rather than measuring polysemantic neurons in a pretrained model.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative outcomes for superposition and feature retention, but no numerical values for these outcomes in the text. It does not measure individual neurons responding to unrelated inputs. Its effective-rank results are about task-level capacity allocation, not neuron polysemanticity; its retention results concern forgetting rather than whether a neuron has one coherent meaning.
record.test_reason: The study measures directional overlap among ground-truth feature embeddings in a 5- or 9-dimensional latent of a toy continual-learning encoder. It does not measure whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs. The authors say superposition 'is not simply a property of neurons.' The bottleneck (m < |It|) is imposed by design, with no no-bottleneck comparison and no neuron-level analysis, so nothing links overlap to neuron polysemanticity. Superposition is used as a concept to study forgetting. The overlap-vs-sparsity result is a related but different construct and is recorded under fits_no_version, not as a test of V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude three things. Sparsity reliably increases superposition, with dips at task boundaries followed by growth. Overlap is harmful mainly for weak, fresh features. Sparser regimes yield higher task-level effective rank. They argue representation strength and capacity allocation, not overlap alone, moderate retention. The paraphrase omits the effective-rank conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a synthetic generator–separator setup, pure-feature probes, directional-overlap metrics, and continual-learning training; it does not reproduce the neuron visualization or circuit-analysis method of the cited vision work.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with sparsity, task-boundary timing, representation strength, and time since first exposure.

fits_no_version.finding: In a bottlenecked toy encoder, sparser ground-truth features are encoded with larger directional overlap S(i,t) among feature embeddings (Figure 2, sparsity 0.15 vs 0.2). This is reported qualitatively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In bottlenecked networks, sparser features are stored with more directional overlap (superposition) in latent space.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature-direction overlap generally rises over sequential training, dipping at task boundaries before recovering (Figure 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During continual learning, superposition grows over time with transient dips at task boundaries.

fits_no_version.finding: SINDy fits indicate retention loss concentrates where representation strength is low and overlap is high. Strong or longer-exposed features are more resilient.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overlapped features are more prone to forgetting only when weakly represented or recently introduced.

fits_no_version.finding: Task-level effective rank of embeddings increases with feature sparsity, with small contractions at task boundaries (Figures 5-6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tasks built from sparser features occupy more latent directions in continual learning.

record.problems: The evidence is from a controlled toy setting rather than real pretrained models or neuron-level responses. The paper's stated limitations include uniform feature sparsity, disjoint task supports, a polynomial SINDy model, and a representation-strength retention proxy that is not direct task performance. The reported outcomes in the main text are qualitative, without numerical values or stated uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows were made for task effective rank because it measures task-level embedding capacity rather than neuron polysemanticity. No separate retention row was linked to V3 because retention loss is not the behavior V3 names.

untested.parts: No vision classifier or neuron-level image responses.
No transformer language models or MLP neurons.

No neuron-level polysemanticity is measured. Capacity pressure (feature/neuron ratio) is not varied, and there is no comparison with a no-bottleneck condition. Only latent-direction overlap under an imposed bottleneck is reported.
No setting with enough neurons for every feature; initialization, regularization and noise are not examined as causes.

Two alternative latent widths (settings 2 and 3) are reported only as robustness checks. Activation functions, architectures and regularization are not compared for polysemantic-neuron share or performance cost.
No interpretability analysis of whether mixed neuron responses share one feature.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V3 'supports' label is removed. The study measures latent-direction overlap in a toy encoder with an imposed bottleneck. It says nothing about neurons being polysemantic or what causes that. All results are qualitative descriptions of figures, with no numbers or uncertainty. It is a preprint.

versions.untested_parts: No vision classifier or image-neuron responses are tested.
No transformer language models, tokens, or contexts are tested.

The study measures overlap among ground-truth feature embeddings in a toy encoder, not polysemantic responses of individual neurons. It does not compare settings with and without capacity pressure or vary the feature-to-neuron ratio.
Initialization, regularization, and training noise as causes of polysemantic neurons without capacity pressure are not tested.

The paper has alternative toy settings, but does not test how activation functions, modern architectures, or regularization change the share of polysemantic neurons or the performance cost of reducing it.
No neuron-level interpretability analysis tests whether mixed responses share a coherent feature.
The study does not compare activation-range choices or explanation-scoring methods for classifying neurons as polysemantic.

rows.subject: encoder Eθ (controlled toy-world model)
rows.operation_detail: Measured superposition strength S(i,t), defined as the aggregate squared projection of other feature embeddings onto feature i's direction.

conditions.value: comparison includes 0.15 and 0.2; higher sparsity regimes are also discussed

rows.value: The text reports systematically larger S(i,t) at higher sparsity.
rows.note: The paper says the encoder uses increased directional sharing as sparsity rises. The model has a latent bottleneck, with m < |It|, but no no-bottleneck comparison is reported.
rows.check: Measures aggregate squared projection of other feature embeddings onto feature i's latent direction, not neuron polysemanticity. The bottleneck is fixed by design, and capacity pressure and feature-to-neuron ratio are not varied. The result is qualitative only, with no numbers or baseline. It cannot show whether neurons are polysemantic because of superposition.

rows.subject: encoder Eθ (controlled toy-world model)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked superposition strength S(i,t) over training time.
rows.measure: Temporal pattern of superposition strength S(i,t)
rows.value: The text reports that superposition generally increases over time, with transient dips at task boundaries followed by recovery and continued growth.
rows.note: This is a qualitative description; no numerical series is given in the text.
rows.check: Tracks the temporal pattern of feature-direction overlap across task boundaries in continual learning. This is a training-dynamics finding about overlap, not about polysemantic neurons or their cause. The result is qualitative only.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
